# v0.30.1-rc1 — recovering the rows of interrupted and failed turns

This is the first release candidate for v0.30.1, a patch release on v0.30.0 and the first v0.30.x release train: it carries the fixes that were ready when the train was cut. It stores two kinds of turns that v0.30.0 could leave only in the host's database: a turn interrupted by a hard kill in a conversation that uses Hermes's legacy rotating compaction, and a Desktop session whose turn failed and that never ended. It also stops a second copy of a saved tool result on the first replay after an upgrade from v0.29.2, links the reply copies that a cold restart stores after an edit-and-resend, and keeps every `snippets` recall response under its size cap.

It adds one setting, `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED` (default `true`). The schema version stays 5, and v0.30.0 remains the latest stable release until this candidate passes its gates (see **Qualification**).

## Changes since v0.30.0

### Restarts and recovery

- **Rows that a hard kill leaves in an abandoned compaction child are recovered.** With Hermes's legacy rotating compaction (`compression.in_place: false`), over ACP on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1, a restart resumes the conversation's parent session and abandons the compaction child that holds the interrupted turn, so LCM-X was never shown those rows. At the next start of that conversation, a background worker now reads that child with the host's own reader and stores the rows LCM-X lacks, only when the child's stored compaction proof covers everything before them. It runs once per process for each bound session and never on a turn. Those turns do not return to the model's view ([#2626](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2626)). `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED=false` turns it off. Its limits are under **Known issues** ([#2624](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2624), [#2632](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2632), picked onto the release branch in [#2671](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2671)).
- **A Desktop session whose turn failed, and that never ended, is stored.** On Hermes v0.23.1, a turn that fails or is stopped before its reply finishes returns without the per-turn hook, and a Desktop session never gets a session end, so when no later turn completed, LCM-X held none of its rows. At a later session start on the same profile, a background job now reads the host's database, read-only, and stores such a session when its last row is the host's failed-turn notice, it is 10 minutes to 7 days old, and LCM-X holds none of its rows. The job runs at most once every 10 minutes for each process, store and home, and never on a turn. When ingest starts a session from its first row, it runs the same check a bind runs, so a session that another process already stored is not stored twice. Forward only: sessions that failed before the upgrade are not stored. The same setting turns it off. Its limits are under **Known issues** ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042), [#2662](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2662), picked onto the release branch in [#2684](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2684)).
- **Reply copies that a cold restart stores after an edit-and-resend are linked.** After an edit-and-resend, a cold restart stores the session's unstamped reply history again. Each copy now carries a `possible_replay_of` link to the stored reply, so the copies are visible instead of silent; nothing is stored or skipped differently. The ingest ledger moving the resume point up from 0 no longer turns this linking off. Pairing those replies within their turn is planned for v0.30.2 ([#2537](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2537)) ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479), [#2529](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2529), picked onto the release branch in [#2664](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2664)).

### Upgrade from v0.29.2

- **The first replay after an upgrade from v0.29.2 no longer stores a saved tool result a second time.** v0.30.0 listed this under **Known issues**: when v0.29.2 had stored a tool result as a bare saved-output marker, in the host's temp results folder (a file with Windows line ends included) or with a data URI in its preview, the first replay stored the tool call and its result once more. The upgrade replay and the session-end compare now use one rule for a bare marker: it is the same row only when the host's marker text is byte-identical once placeholders are restored and redaction is applied on both sides, with no recovery from the saved file. For such rows the store keeps the marker v0.29.2 stored, not the saved file's content, as it already did for the plain case ([#2521](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2521)). This holds with sensitive-pattern redaction on or off. A result that the host sends as one text part is not covered yet; see **Known issues**. One copy remains, listed under **Known issues** ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558), [#2584](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2584) and [#2663](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2663), picked together onto the release branch in [#2674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2674)). The counts and scope of that named limit in `docs/exactly-once-ingest.md` are corrected to match ([#2677](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2677), picked in [#2678](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2678)).

### Ingest

- **Some ingests hold the write lock for less time.** The identity-anchor presence check now returns before any read when it has nothing to check: no tool call or result among its candidates, and no rewritten row to exclude. Both of its outcomes then give the same result, so those reads only lengthened the write-lock hold. On the bench, this step alone cut the probe's median hold from 433 to 392 ms. It is one step of the busy-database work ([#2293](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2293)); the rest is planned for v0.30.2 (see the busy-session item under **Known issues**) ([#2644](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2644), picked onto the release branch in [#2665](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2665)).

### Recall

- **Every `snippets` recall response fits under its size cap.** A `snippets` response could pass the 64,000-character response cap once the query echo, provenance and markers around the hits were counted. Every `snippets` path now budgets the whole response, with snippet windows off or on, skipped reads and extra entries included: an oversized response with no hits cuts its query echo to its first 4,096 characters and reports `query_truncated`, and full hits are dropped from the end in rank order with `response_cap_truncated`. A per-call limit too large for an integer, such as `1e999`, now falls back to the default instead of raising an error. Responses that already fit, and stored rows, are unchanged. v0.30.0 listed both defects under **Known issues** ([#2620](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2620), ported onto the release branch in [#2670](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2670)).

### Testing improved

- **New regression tests** for each fix above: compaction-child recovery and its review cases; the failed-turn catch-up and its ingest check; the restart after an edit-and-resend; the bare-marker identity on stores that v0.29.2 wrote, plus a check that such a replay stores no fewer rows than v0.30.0; and the `snippets` response cap.
- **Real-host test fixes:** three tests that failed on real host builds in v0.30.0's host-suite run, each for a reason in the test, are fixed: one removed the host variables from the rest of the test process, one waited for a log line that ingest no longer writes, and one assumed path filtering hides an editable install. A new guard fails any test that changes an `LCM_REAL_*` variable ([#2636](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2636), [#2637](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2637), [#2638](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2638), [#2660](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2660), picked onto the release branch in [#2666](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2666)).

## On by default in this release

Every change above is on by default. The one new setting, `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED`, turns off both recovery paths and their reads of the host's database. Everything else keeps v0.30.0's defaults, including the ingest ledger in `shadow` mode and local semantic recall.

## Upgrade

- **Host and Python.** As in v0.30.0: Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is required (0.21.5 or newer recommended), with Python 3.11 or newer. The compaction-child recovery applies on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1 and the failed-turn catch-up on Hermes v0.23.1.
- **Store schema.** The schema version stays 5, with no new tables or columns. Each recovered row carries one metadata entry (`host_row_recovered:<store_id>` or `unended_turn_recovered:<store_id>`) that nothing in the product reads. The failed-turn catch-up also writes one marker per host home (`unended_catchup_since:<hash>`), which sets the time it starts from; the marker survives a rollback and a re-upgrade, and v0.30.0 ignores it.
- **New setting.** `LCM_HOST_ROW_RECOVERY_ENABLED` (default `true`). Set it to `false` to turn off the compaction-child recovery and the failed-turn catch-up, and their host reads; with it off, LCM-X behaves as v0.30.0 does on these paths.
- **From v0.29.2 or older:** read the v0.30.0 upgrade notes first: the ingest ledger, the removed settings, the identity-anchor switch and the rollback limit.
- **Rollback.** Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`). The rollback target is v0.30.0. The schema does not change, and rows that v0.30.1 recovered stay in the store as ordinary rows. After a rollback, v0.30.0's own behaviour and its **Known issues** apply to that store again, and two items under **Known issues** below still apply to the rows v0.30.1 recovered: a compaction child resumed by its own id is stored again ([#2630](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2630)), and recovered rows can be stored out of order ([#2672](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2672)). The upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade row runs in the smoke stage, and the GA notes report its result.
- **If you ran v0.30.0 on a store that v0.29.2 had written.** The copies that v0.30.0 stored on the first replay after that upgrade stay in the store: v0.30.1 does not remove them ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558)).

## Known issues

Loss limits come first. Fixes are planned for v0.30.x unless a different release is named. “Resume point” means the position through which LCM-X believes it has already examined the host’s messages.

- **An interrupted helper agent can lose the rows after its last save.** A helper agent's rows are saved before each of its model calls; the hook waits at most 2 seconds for the save, which then finishes in the background. A save that cannot finish (a database that stays busy, an error) leaves its rows to the helper agent's next save or its end. If the process ends before a save has stored them, the rows since the last stored save are not saved. This happens while its tools run: that round's tool call and finished results stay only in the host's database. It also happens while a save waits more than 5 seconds on a busy database at shutdown, and then one WARNING gives the number of rows not yet saved. Every earlier row is saved for a helper agent that runs its own LCM-X engine, while that engine still serves the profile the helper agent started with. Otherwise, and for a helper agent without its own engine, the rows not yet saved are saved only when the helper agent finishes, so an interruption loses them, as before v0.30.0. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2482](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2482), [#2483](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2483)).
- **New messages after a host-shortened history are lost.** If the host shortens the conversation on its own, such as an undo followed by a compression request that compacts nothing, later new messages are treated as already stored and are not saved. Which hosts produce this shape is not established. A second known route is Hermes's message-sequence repair, which runs only when message alternation is broken and rewrites the list in place: if LCM-X ingests the repaired, shorter list before the next new message, that next user message is not stored. No run has shown this route yet. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1525](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1525)).
- **Repeated text is under-stored on partial-history hosts.** After a restart and compaction, a host that sends only new messages loses occurrences of text repeated within the session. The reference agent sends full history. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)).
- **Repeated compacted-out tool pairs are lost.** On hosts that reuse tool-call IDs, a new call and result identical to a pair compacted out of view are treated as a replay after a cold restart and are not stored. The already-shipped fix for a pair still in view does not cover this shape. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **Busy session end with undo and resend leaves a message unstored.** With ignore patterns configured, a busy session end followed by undo, resend and an ingest that changes nothing leaves the earlier occurrence pending and counted at exit, but not stored ([#2247](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2247)). Separately, without ignore patterns, any busy session end followed by an undo and resend also keeps the earlier occurrence pending, counted and reported at exit rather than stored. Only a host resume of that session recovers it; `/new` does not. ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838), [#2206](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2206)). Planned fix: v0.30.x.
- **An ignored-message placeholder makes a later loss silent.** If ignore patterns are or were configured and the session-end view contains an LCM-X ignored-message placeholder, a busy session end followed by undo and resend loses the earlier occurrence. Session end logs a pending retry, but the later drop is neither counted nor reported. v0.29.x lost the same message on this trigger but warned at session end that final messages might be missing; v0.30.0 no longer gives that warning. No ignore patterns are set by default. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2474](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2474)).
- **Untimestamped replacements before the resume point are lost.** A host merge or replacement before the resume point drops an unstamped new row; if an entirely unstamped view replaces all rows at the same length, none of the new rows is stored. On Hermes this follows undoing every turn or retrying a one-turn session when no host database exists or its transcript write failed; timestamped rows are stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#7](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/7)).
- **Some moved tool rows are still skipped.** A moved tool call or result before the resume point is not rescued when the audit finds no missing row there. The audit never examines tool rows on its own: a tool call and result replaced before the resume point are lost, and a pair inserted there stores its result without its call ([#2452](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2452)). Tool groups that cross the resume point while their unstamped results were already stored also retain the old skip behaviour. Affected new rows are not stored; planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467); fixed in v0.30.0 on turns where the audit also misses a row inside the presence window, [#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455)).
- **Large or non-standard tool histories keep the old loss behaviour.** The moved-tool check does not run beyond 10,000 stored rows, 15 million bytes of stored text or 10,000 tool-call entries across the session and its ancestry. It also falls back for the whole scope if any stored tool-call format is non-standard: call entries must be objects with text IDs and text arguments. New moved rows left classified as positional replays are not stored, and one INFO line reports the limit; planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467); fixed in v0.30.0 on turns where the audit also misses a row inside the presence window, [#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455)).
- **Externalized arguments and reused IDs bypass the moved-tool fix.** A call whose arguments are externalized at ingest reads as a reused ID, including an inline data URI with at least 256 base64 characters, a run of at least 4,096 base64-alphabet characters, or line-wrapped base64. Reused IDs, repeated call or result IDs in the view, and argument comparisons beyond the 256,000-byte parsing budget retain the old replay decision, leaving affected new call or result rows unstored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172), [#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Replaced unstamped replies and scaffold-looking replies are lost.** If a reply reaches LCM-X without its host timestamp and the host replaces it before the resume point (an edit-and-resend in a long session), the replacement is not stored while the session runs. A restart stores it, together with copies of the session's other unstamped replies ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479)). Replies that carry their host timestamp, as Hermes sends them unless a session has no host database or a transcript write failed, are stored. Planned fix for this part: v0.30.x ([#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116)). A reply carrying `CONTEXT SUMMARY` markers is still treated as LCM-X scaffold while the engine is running, and lossy-redacted rows still count as replays. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Unreadable ancestry limits moved-row recovery.** If presence reads fail, ancestry cannot be verified with `state.db` present, or a rotation-predecessor write failed in the current process, only rows found by the existing audit are stored. Other rows before the resume point remain classified as replays and affected new rows are not stored; a warning reports the fallback. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Identifier-only replacements behind a merged summary are lost.** When the host changes only a message’s unique ID behind an unchanged merged scaffold, the cached prefix consumes the proof and the replacement is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1428](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1428)).
- **A new occurrence at an alternate timestamp is lost.** Once the original host view is gone, a new event with identical content at a previously recorded alternate timestamp is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1519](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1519)).
- **Earlier edits inside a shortened view are lost.** If a host shortens its view and edits an earlier row in place, LCM-X does not store that edit. This also occurs in v0.27.0. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1563](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1563)).
- **A retried result with only a new ID is lost.** After a cold restart, a retried tool result whose only change is its unique message ID is dropped. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837)).
- **Identical new tool pairs after restart are lost.** A new call and result identical to an earlier stored pair are treated as a replay after restart and are not stored. If the restart follows a stored rewrite of the earlier result, the old call is also stored again beside that rewritten result without a replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2377](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2377), [#2414](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2414)).
- **Pasted scaffold-shaped user turns are lost.** A user turn that starts with the preserved-objective prefix or quotes a whole summary part is skipped when there is no current version-4 compaction proof, including before any compaction, under older proofs or after a cold rebind retires a stale proof. A task-list-prefix turn is affected in every proof state; before any compaction, such turns are skipped after restart even at the tail, or while running when before a stored row. From v0.30.1 the task-list case also reaches an engine that bound on an empty store after another writer stored the session's rows (the catch-up path of [#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042), below), which now reconciles as a restart does; that includes a host composite that carries the user's question. Planned fix: v0.30.2 for the task-list case and v0.30.x for the rest ([#2110](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2110), [#2418](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2418)).
- **Equal user identities hide a new occurrence.** In a delegated helper agent's session with many equal user messages, after a restart, a failed compaction step or a host head rewrite, a recorded boundary that becomes ambiguous on the next view lets an older copy count against a new one. One occurrence is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2422](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2422)).
- **A warm view that starts with a tool call can store nothing.** When a warm ingest gets a view that starts with a tool call and does not extend the previous view, none of its rows is stored. No host path is known to produce this view. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2419](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2419)).
- **Non-busy pre-compaction write failures lose child rows.** When a delegated child’s input write fails for a reason other than a locked or busy database, such as a disk or I/O error, compaction still removes rows from its view and those raw rows are lost. Their stored summary is the only trace, and `compression boundary not recorded: input not stored` warns about the failure. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Multiple timestamp conflicts after busy session end lose messages.** After a busy session end with no later ingest, two or more messages whose host timestamps conflict with saved copies can be lost. If a later ingest brings the same messages unchanged, they are kept and counted instead. v0.29.2 has the same limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x.
- **A same-second resend under a new platform ID is lost.** After a cold restart, a new turn with the same text in the same second as an earlier one, under a new platform ID, is taken as the earlier turn and is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1037](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1037)).
- **A repeated tool step after a rewind can be missed, with an identical message after it.** After a restart, if a conversation was rewound and the agent repeats exactly the same tool call with the same result, followed by a message identical to an earlier saved one, all three are taken as a replay and are not saved, even when the host's timestamps show they are new. We know of no way to trigger this from Hermes today. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2259](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2259)).
- **One half of a re-dated tool pair can be saved without the other.** After a restart in a conversation that LCM-X has compacted, if the host re-dates only one half of a saved tool call and its result as new, that half is saved and its partner is not. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2191](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2191)).
- **Messages pending at a busy session end are missing after a gateway stop until you resume.** If a session end found the database busy and the gateway stops before a retry succeeds, the messages still pending are missing from the store until you resume that conversation. After /new they are not recovered. The only sign is the warning logged when the session ended. The fix needs a change in Hermes ([#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)).
- **Under heavy two-writer contention, a session end finds the database busy more often than on v0.29.2.** Our busy-session check with a second writer failed: 19 of 20 session ends were busy against 13 of 20 on v0.29.2 (the limit is 18), and 18 of 20 against 12 of 20 (limit 16) on v0.30.0's last candidate with the partial fix that this release carries (see **Ingest** above). On a 2,000-row batch the write lock is held about 2.3 times as long (2.29 against a 2.25 tripwire, also a FAIL; 1.8 times on a first batch), and the second writer’s ingest waits about 1.4 times as long at p95 on that bench. A busy session end keeps its last messages in memory and stores them at the next session start or end, at shutdown or at a normal exit. They are lost if the process is killed or crashes first, or if the database stays busy through the exit retry (the gateway-stop case is [#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)), and v0.30.0 opens that window more often than v0.29.2. This release does not carry the rest of the fix, and its busy-session check runs on this candidate (see **Qualification**). The fix is planned for v0.30.2 ([#2293](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2293), [#2680](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2680)).
- **Messages can be missing if the database stays busy from a session end until the process ends.** If the database is busy when a session ends, stays busy at every later retry (the next session start or end, a related session's start, and the 5-second shutdown drain), and the process then dies or exits while it is still busy, the session's last messages are not saved. They are saved only if you resume that conversation; /new does not recover them. Every busy session end and every failed retry is logged and counted. This is an accepted limit; fixing it needs a journal outside the database.
- **A few restart cases keep messages pending instead of saving them.** After a busy session end, LCM-X keeps a conversation's newest messages pending, rather than risk saving them in the wrong place, in three more cases: a single message that the host re-dates newer than its saved copy; a view rewritten after later messages were saved; and, when the session's binding is ignored or stateless, a message with a different known timestamp. Pending messages are counted and reported at engine shutdown or a normal exit (not after a gateway stop; see [#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)), but they are saved only if you resume that conversation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838)).
- **An identical message re-sent in place is taken as a replay.** On hosts that send no message IDs or timestamps, a message re-sent with exactly the same text in the same place, so the conversation does not get longer, cannot be told apart from a replay, and it is not saved again. The same holds when a shortened conversation grows back with identical messages, and for identical overlapping messages in a migration or a full-history replay. This is a design limit: telling them apart needs message IDs or timestamps from the host.
- **Some Desktop sessions whose turn failed can still end with nothing saved.** v0.30.1 stores a Desktop session whose turn failed or was stopped, and that never ended, at a later session start on the same profile (see **Changes since v0.30.0**). A session whose failure is older than the profile's first catch-up after the upgrade is not stored; a repair command is planned ([#2652](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2652)). A failed session with no later session start on its profile within 7 days, or with more than 500 rows, also stays only in the host's database. The catch-up stores nothing for a session that has a parent (a delegated, fork or compaction child), that a subagent ran, that ended by compaction, that matches the ignore or stateless session patterns, that holds a row the host has compacted or marked inactive, or whose rows fail its checks: a row with a role other than user, assistant or tool (a `session_meta` or `system` row included), a malformed or duplicate tool call id, a tool result without its call or answered twice, a tool call left unanswered, an ignored message, or a last row that is not the assistant's failed-turn notice. It also skips a session in which LCM-X already holds rows, so a failed last turn after stored turns, with no later turn and no session end, stays only in the host's database ([#2693](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2693)). It retries later, while the session stays eligible, a session that this process has bound, that the host changes while it reads it, or whose read or store fails. Each job reads at most the 64 newest eligible sessions and stores at most 16 of them; the rest wait for a later job, and on a profile with more than 64 such sessions within 7 days, the older ones are not read ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042)).
- **A first turn stopped during a tool round is not stored** in a session that never continues or ends: the host leaves no failed-turn notice for it, so the catch-up does not pick it up. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2653](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2653)).
- **The last rows of a session can be lost when its end is not written at once.** When a session ends while another session is the active one, or while the store is busy, LCM-X stores its last rows only if the rows it already holds match what the host sends. They do not match if the host changed an earlier message of that session. An earlier row that holds an inline encoded block (line-wrapped base64, or a data URI, inside a tool call's arguments or inside list-form content) can also fail that comparison, even when the host re-sends it unchanged, because LCM-X moved the block out at ingest. The rows after that point, usually the final reply, are then not stored. When another session was the active one, no warning is logged; at most an INFO line says the session was skipped. When the store was busy, LCM-X warns that the end is queued for a retry, warns once more when the retry finds the mismatch, keeps the rows pending, and counts and reports them as not stored at a normal exit. This also occurs in v0.29.2, which in addition can lose the final reply when the store is busy at a session's end, even without such a block. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2543](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2543)).
- **A saved tool result replaced in place keeps its first content.** If a host replaced a large tool result in place, under the same call ID and with the same size and opening text, LCM-X keeps the content it stored first and does not store the new content. For a session that ended while another was active this is the same as v0.29.2. It also applies to the rows of a delegated helper agent, which v0.30.0 stores for the first time. No supported Hermes path is known to replace a result this way, from a reading of Hermes's tool-result storage code ([#2544](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2544)).
- **A turn with a tool call nested about 2,000 levels deep is not stored.** If a tool call's arguments are JSON nested about twice Python's recursion limit deep (2,000 levels with the default limit of 1,000), LCM-X fails while reading them. No row of that turn is stored, and no later turn is stored while that call stays in the history the host sends. For a delegated helper agent no row of that handover is stored, and none of any later handover that still holds the call; rows from earlier handovers stay stored. The host sees no error; the only trace is a warning in the log. No real tool call is known to nest this deep, but nothing prevents one. This needs Python 3.12 or later; on Python 3.11 the arguments stay unparsed text and the turn is stored. The main-session case also occurs in v0.29.2. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2583](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2583)).
- **When a host replaces an unanswered tool call under the same call ID, a new call that differs only in how a number is written is taken as the stored call.** LCM-X can store a tool call at the start of a turn, before its result exists. If the host then sends that turn again with a call under the same ID whose arguments differ from the stored ones only in the spelling of a number, and both spellings read as the same 64-bit float, LCM-X keeps the stored call, does not store the new call's row, and stores its result. That is intended for one number written two ways (1.0 and 1.00). It also happens for two different numbers that read as one float: 0.1 and 0.10000000000000001, or 1e400 and 2e400. v0.29.2 stores neither the new call nor its result in this case. No supported Hermes version is known to replace a call under the same ID. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **With payload externalization turned off, a saved tool result is not recognised as the stored row.** This needs a non-default setting (`LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_EXTERNALIZATION_ENABLED=false`). LCM-X then stores the marker of a saved tool result with lines of its own added, and that row never matches the marker the host sends again, so the saved-result matching of v0.30.0 does not apply. When such a session ends while another session is the active one, or while the store is busy, the rows after that result, usually the final reply, are not stored. v0.29.2 loses the same rows with this setting. In a delegated helper agent's session the result is also still stored again on each model call, with nothing marking the copies. Keep payload externalization on, as it is by default. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2547](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2547)).
- **With redaction on, a result saved in the system temp folder can cost a session its last rows.** Sensitive-pattern redaction is off by default. With it on, when the preview of a tool result that Hermes saved in the system temp folder holds text that redaction rewrites, LCM-X cannot pair the stored row with the marker Hermes sends again. If that session ends while another session is the active one, the rows that arrive with its end, usually the final reply, are not stored. v0.29.2 does the same. Hermes saved results there only up to 0.20.4, and LCM-X supports Hermes 0.21.3 and later, so no supported setup is affected; a result saved under Hermes's home is not affected ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).
- **The rows of a turn interrupted by a hard kill are recovered only when the conversation starts again, and only under a strict proof.** Only in a conversation that has a compaction child (Hermes's legacy rotating compaction, `compression.in_place: false`; the default is in-place compaction), over ACP on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1. v0.30.1 recovers those rows at the next start of that conversation (see **Changes since v0.30.0**). A conversation that is never loaded again keeps them only in the host's database, on any host and in any mode. A compaction child whose stored proof does not strictly cover the rows before them stores nothing, logs one warning per process and is read again at each start; one whose remaining rows hold an ignored row, an orphaned tool result or a damaged tool group also stores nothing. Rows the host's own reader does not return are not recovered, and rows it rewrites are stored as it returns them. A compaction child that LCM-X never bound, and hosts and transports other than the tested ones, are not covered ([#2624](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2624)).
- **A rare message loss after two compactions in a row is under investigation** ([#2330](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2330)): in one run of the reliability test matrix, two messages that arrived right after a compaction rotated the session were never stored, because a second compaction ran in the new session before the turn ended. It has not been reproduced: the failing cell was repeated 8 times on the same host with full logging, and all 8 passed. v0.29.2's notes list the same lead. If it recurs, that run's stores and logs are kept for the fix, which ships in a later release.
- **A hook-only delegated child can rebind its parent's engine.** This is traced in the source only: it has never been observed, and no test covers it yet. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2066](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2066)).
- **A store that a v0.30.0 release candidate wrote can still lose a session's last rows.** A row that a candidate stored while its payload file could not be written, or with redaction on, keeps that form, and a session that holds it can lose its last rows when it ends while another session is active; an early candidate's session can be missing its last rows for good. See **Upgrade** in the v0.30.0 notes. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).

These loss shapes are also tracked, each in its own issue, which sets its fix release:

- **A new user turn that starts with a summary prefix is skipped.** LCM-X takes it for its own summary carrier and does not store it ([#1003](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1003)).
- **Rows appended after a shorter host view are not stored when they carry no host timestamps.** The fix needs the next-stage message classifier ([#1547](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1547), [#2058](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2058)).
- **The next-stage message classifier has six correctness defects.** They are to be fixed before it is wired into ingest; no path reaches them today ([#2288](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2288)).
- **A host startup stall past the 10 s deadline leaves LCM-X inactive.** No session in that host process is stored until the host restarts or the plugin is reloaded ([#2339](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2339)).
- **On an upgraded store with blank conversation IDs, a legacy row lets another conversation claim its receipt** ([#2423](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2423)).
- **In a session shared by two conversations, a new tool row is not stored** ([#2442](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2442)).
- **Rewrite-memory eviction after 16 notes can lose a merged prompt.** No supported path to 16 notes has been found ([#2476](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2476)).
- **Three routes can send rows to the wrong store if two profiles share one module copy.** Hermes loads one copy per home ([#2499](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2499)).
- **A host that edited a handed-over message in place could have the original skipped.** The ledger binds a digest taken before its transaction. No host writer is known to do this ([#2500](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2500)).
- **A cross-room /resume leaves the fold or snapshot owned by the old conversation** ([#2501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2501)).
- **A partial summary deletion at /new leaves stored rows that no summary covers.** This is summary coverage, not a stored-row loss: the rows stay stored ([#2045](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2045)).

The remaining limits store extra copies, leave attribution incomplete, fail to honour an exclusion rule, slow a turn or store rows out of order. They do not lose raw rows.

- **Some excluded parents still have stored children.** After an excluded parent rotates through compression, its delegated child is refused only on the shared route. Clone and prototype routes store the child despite `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` or the stateless exclusion patterns. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2070](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2070)).
- **Failed pre-compaction storage also duplicates a head.** After a failed input write before compaction, LCM-X stores the compacted head once more without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Repeated recovery stores a user row again.** Two recovery fits of a repeated user turn followed by a restart store the projected user row once more, without a replay relation. Fix release not yet set ([#503](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/503)).
- **A later child restart stores kept rows again.** After rejecting a delegated child’s last-stored-row resume boundary, an identical rewritten view stores kept rows again without a replay relation. This takes one restart after a warm rejection or a second restart after a cold rejection; delegated-child restart resume is not reachable on the current host. The record of a child's last compaction outputs is also kept only in memory, so a restart of a delegated child stores its compacted head one extra time. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2439](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2439)).
- **Routing-key changes store the history again.** If the host assigns a live session a new routing key, such as a CLI handoff or resume from another room, the next warm turn stores the whole history again under the new conversation ID without replay relations. This was found in clone-run preflight and code reading and is not yet reproduced on main. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2461](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2461)).
- **Missing compression ancestry duplicates carried rows.** When a compression child’s ancestry cannot be verified and the host inserts a row before the resume point, the next ingest stores the parent’s final prompt and reply again without replay relations. This includes missing host state, missing parent or child records, a parent that did not end by compression or a fork marker; apparently complete ancestry also fails when an earlier process never wrote a needed predecessor record. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2463](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2463)).
- **A merged summary carrier creates an extra copy.** After the host merges LCM-X’s summary carrier into a user row, a warm replay from the start stores the merged carrier again, or stores copies from an otherwise unchanged view plus appended rows. Other middle-of-history edits do not belong to this limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1961](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1961)).
- **An unstamped restart replay stores old rows again.** The first ingest after restart can store another copy while advancing past a replayed prefix. This limit requires matching earlier rows in order, an earlier timestamped copy and a new copy with `observed_at` NULL; replay from position zero is handled by the new replay-link fix. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A rewritten unstamped view is stored again.** An ended engine’s final flush stores an unstamped view again after a resumed engine rewrites it, or a rewrite after a cold-start retry is stored again. A view with an additional host insertion or reordering is outside this limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2203](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2203)).
- **An unanswered prompt becomes part of a composite.** After a restart before the reply, the unanswered prompt and the next prompt are stored together as a composite row beside the next prompt’s own row. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#849](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/849)).
- **Rotation mapping can stall compaction.** A rotation leaves rows without the mapping compaction needs, so compaction stops making progress. A cold resend after a held fit-only rotation also stores predecessor rows again; those copies now carry `possible_replay_of` links across the recorded rotation chain, except the re-emitted summary marker. Planned fix for the remaining mapping and store-growth limits: v0.30.x ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Unstamped histories with existing copies grow on every restart.** On a host that sends no message timestamps, a session that already holds later exact copies of some rows stores its replayed history once more at each restart. Each extra copy has a possible-replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#588](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/588)).
- **Earlier ledger-off copies cannot anchor borrowed-timestamp links.** Borrowed-timestamp linking cannot see a copy stored while `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER` was off. It can therefore link to a different bound copy when complete bindings would have left the attribution ambiguous; no row or per-key count changes. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2443](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2443)).
- **A late tool call stores its result twice.** When a tool call's row was not stored at its turn, a later ingest that brings the call (typically after a restart or a rebind, when the host sends its full history) stores the call once and its result a second time, without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2468](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2468)).
- **A persistent evidence fault can store the last row again.** After an evidence-read fault that persists past its retry (or a busy error followed by a one-off evidence-read fault, which gets no retry), the fail-open path can store the already-stored last row once more, shifted by a timestamped insert before it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2374](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2374)).
- **Unstamped reply histories are stored again after an edit-and-resend and a restart.** On a host that sends replies without timestamps, a cold restart after an edit-and-resend stores the session's whole unstamped reply history again (41 copies after 40 turns in our test). From v0.30.1 each copy is linked to the stored reply with `possible_replay_of`, so the copies are visible, not silent; nothing is stored or skipped differently. Replies with host timestamps are not affected, and v0.29.1 and v0.29.2 store the same copies, without links. Pairing those replies within their turn is planned for v0.30.2 ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479), [#2537](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2537)).
- **A new reply with the same text as an earlier reply can be marked as a possible copy.** After an edit-resend, when a cold restart links the reply copies it stores again, a genuinely new reply with the same text as an earlier reply can also be marked as a possible copy of it. The reply is stored and delivered as usual, and nothing hides or skips a row because of the mark ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479)).
- **A restart right after a fit-only compaction can save the summary again.** After a compaction that only trimmed the conversation to fit, if the host keeps the trimmed list and the agent restarts before LCM-X next saves the session, one extra copy of LCM-X's summary joined to the first kept message can be saved as a plain message. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2118](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2118)).
- **A to-do list merged with your next message can be saved again.** The host can merge a saved to-do list with your next message into one combined message. When that combined message splits cleanly into earlier saved messages of the same session, LCM-X now links it to them with `composite_of`. After a conversation ends and resumes, though, the combined message is saved again with no link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2488](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2488)).
- **A message can be saved twice after certain compaction passes.** After an overflow-recovery pass, or a compaction whose compacted messages were all hidden ones, if the host commits the rewritten conversation and restarts before the next compaction, a message can be saved again with no replay link. This has not been reproduced yet. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2134](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2134)).
- **A reused tool-call ID far apart can save a pair twice after a restart.** If a session reuses a tool-call ID for the same call and result more than 64 saved rows later, a restart can save that pair a second time without a replay link. No natural way to trigger this has been shown; our test forces it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2197](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2197)).
- **A failed hand-off read can save a carried message again.** If LCM-X cannot read the previous session's record during a hand-off, a carried-over message can be saved again without a replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2490](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2490)).
- **A kept message with a model-switch note can be saved again.** After a compaction, when the conversation is picked up again, a kept message that starts with a model-switch note and is shown with an extra leading space can be saved again, along with the next carried-over message. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2431](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2431)).
- **Older databases without conversation IDs can save a tool pair twice.** On older databases with no conversation IDs recorded, a tool call and its result can be saved twice after a restart. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2436](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2436)).
- **An insert into a just-compacted conversation can save the latest reply again.** If the app inserts a message without a timestamp into a conversation that a compaction has just moved to a new session, and the latest reply also has no timestamp, LCM-X can save that reply a second time. Without the app's session database, the carried-over earlier prompts can be saved again too. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2491](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2491), [#2463](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2463)).
- **A few compaction and setting-change paths save a marked extra copy.** After certain compactions, a restart can save LCM-X's summary or the compacted input again, marked as a copy: when the compaction's saved record is out of date, when a compaction that moved the conversation to a new session (a non-default setting) is followed by a restart before the new session starts, or when a restart comes before a new compaction is adopted. Changing the redaction setting before LCM-X first saves a session with the ingest ledger on can also save one marked extra copy, once. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286), [#758](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/758)).
- **A tool call with a long wrapped encoded block can be stored again at each restart.** A tool call whose arguments hold line-wrapped base64 of 4,096 characters or more, and its result, are stored once more at every cold restart in two cases: on a store written before v0.30.0; and, on any store, after the host changed that call's arguments in place. A call that v0.30.0 stored itself and that the host sends again unchanged is stored once. No row is lost; in the measurement in #2550, at most the first extra copy was linked as a possible replay, and the other copies were not marked. No supported Hermes version is known to change a stored call's arguments. Both cases also occur in v0.29.2. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2550](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2550)).
- **Rolling back to v0.29.2 stores a saved tool result once more.** v0.30.0 stores the full content of a tool result that Hermes saved to a file. v0.29.2 knows such a result only as its short marker, so after a rollback it stores the tool call and the marker once more, the first time the host replays that history. Nothing is lost. The copy is not linked to the first one, and it does not grow on later replays or on upgrading again. Planned: link these copies on re-upgrade, in v0.30.2 ([#2552](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2552)).
- **A saved tool result that was stored as its marker stays a marker.** v0.29.2 stored a large tool result that Hermes had saved to a file as the short marker Hermes leaves in the conversation. After the upgrade, LCM-X keeps that row as it is and does not add the saved file's content. From v0.30.1 this also holds for the upgrade cases that v0.30.0 stored a second time (see **Changes since v0.30.0**), apart from the copy listed below. The same holds for a result whose file was missing when v0.30.0 first stored it, for one whose payload file LCM-X could not write then, and, with sensitive-pattern redaction on, for a result saved under Hermes's home whose preview held text that redaction rewrites: the row stays a marker afterwards. The marker and its preview are what the model was shown; nothing the host sent is lost. Other results whose file is present when v0.30.0 stores them are stored in full ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **A reused call ID with an identical marker can be stored once more.** If a host reuses a tool call ID and repeats the identical saved-output marker, and the store holds that marker as a marker (see the item above), a replay that starts at a different point in the history stores one more copy of it. This happens once; a later replay adds nothing, and no host row is lost. No supported Hermes version is known to reuse a call ID this way ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **After an upgrade from v0.29.2, a saved tool result can be stored once more when the host reuses its call id.** After an upgrade from v0.29.2, a tool call whose result is stored as a bare saved-output marker can be stored once more when the host later reuses that call id with the identical marker. v0.30.0 already stores the same copy at the first replay; v0.30.1 stores it at a later replay and never holds more rows than v0.30.0. Nothing is lost ([#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558)).
- **After an upgrade from v0.29.2, a replayed tool result sent as one text part can still be stored a second time** when v0.29.2 stored its saved-output marker bare. Nothing is lost. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2521](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2521)).
- **A helper agent's saved tool result can be stored one extra time.** LCM-X normally recognises a saved tool result by its marker. When a helper agent's history no longer lines up with its stored rows (the host trimmed or rewrote it, or after the helper agent's own compaction), LCM-X matches rows by counting them and compares the result's content instead. There, a result whose saved file is missing or was rewritten, or a reused tool call ID, is stored one extra time in total. No row is lost ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **A helper agent's row with an inline encoded block is stored more than once.** When a delegated helper agent's tool call holds an inline encoded block in its arguments, or a list-form row holds one in its content, LCM-X moves the block out when it stores the row, and at the next handover the stored row no longer matches what the host sends. The row is then stored again: one extra copy in a live helper session and at its end, up to two where rows are matched by counting, and up to three after the helper agent's own compaction. The copies stop after the second handover, and no row is lost. v0.29.2 does not store helper-agent sessions at all. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2559](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2559)).
- **With redaction on, a saved tool result whose preview holds redacted text is kept as its marker, and its conversation can be stored again after a restart.** Sensitive-pattern redaction is off by default. With it on, a tool result saved under Hermes's home whose preview holds text that redaction rewrites is stored as its marker: LCM-X keeps the marker and its preview, not the saved file's full text. When the preview ends inside a secret, a first part of it that is too short for a pattern to match stays in the stored preview. On a replay after a restart whose assistant and tool rows carry no timestamps, rows of that conversation can then be stored again, at each such replay; v0.29.2 stores the same rows or more. A replay that carries timestamps on every row stores nothing twice, except when the rewritten text is a password, which redaction replaces without keeping a fingerprint, and the replay sends only part of the history; rows are then stored again, fewer than in v0.29.2. No row is lost. v0.29.2 also keeps only the marker and its preview, with the same short first part. A store that the release candidates rc1 to rc5 wrote with redaction on has two more effects, described under **Upgrade** in the v0.30.0 notes. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604)).
- **While LCM-X cannot write its payload files, a replayed conversation that holds a saved tool result can be stored again.** If payload files cannot be written for a longer time (a full disk, or a payload folder that cannot be written to) while the database stays writable, a replay after a restart that sends only part of the history, and whose assistant and tool rows carry no timestamps, stores rows of such a conversation again at each replay, as v0.29.2 does. After the fault clears, a replay that sends only part of the history stores rows once more, and only once: with timestamps on every row, the tool call and its result, or the result alone when the replay starts at the result; without timestamps on assistant and tool rows, three rows, or two when the replay starts at the result. For a result under Hermes's home, v0.29.2 stores nothing again in the first case and stores rows again at every replay in the second. No row is lost ([#2605](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2605)).
- **A conversation stored with payload externalization turned off can be stored again on a replay.** Payload externalization is on by default. For a conversation that was stored with it off and holds a saved tool result, a replay after a restart stores rows of it again in 7 of the 12 replay forms tested: 5 with it still off, and 2 after it was turned on again. The copies can grow with each replay. No row is lost. v0.29.2 stores the same or more in every form. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2597](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2597)).
- **One slow first turn after a restart on an affected session.** When one stored tool row carries only a name, the check at a cold start holds the store's write lock for about 4.3 s on a 2,000-row session in our measurement (an upper bound, taken on a shared machine). No data is affected. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2258](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2258)).
- **The opt-in event recorder can keep one database file open until cleanup.** When the recorder replaces its database connection or hits a read error, it drops the old connection without closing it, so the file handle stays open until Python’s garbage collection runs. No data is affected. The recorder is off by default. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2642](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2642)).
- **A crash after a compaction rotation, over ACP on upstream Hermes, can store one user turn twice.** The fault cells show it on both v0.29.2 and v0.30.0. Fix release not yet set ([#2507](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2507)).
- **After a crash during an upgrade from v0.27.0, a composite row is kept beside its replayed parts.** The fault cells show it on both v0.29.2 and v0.30.0 ([#1506](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1506)).
- **An equal-identity omission alignment can store a kept row twice.** This is the part of #1451 that stays open for v0.30.x ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
- **A compaction child resumed later by its own id is stored again.** If a compaction child whose rows v0.30.1 recovered is later resumed by its exact id without its conversation key (a CLI resume by the child's id, or a TUI lazy resume; not ACP or the gateway), it is bound into a new conversation and its whole list is stored there, copies of the recovered rows included. Nothing is lost ([#2630](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2630)).
- **Recovered rows can be stored out of order.** When the host later resumes a compaction child whose rows v0.30.1 recovered, and re-sends an earlier turn of that child with a changed timestamp or message ID, the recovered question and reply end up ahead of that re-sent turn in store order, instead of after it. Order only: the stored rows match v0.30.0's, with none lost or stored twice. Planned fix: v0.30.2 ([#2672](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2672)).

Duplicate attribution requires the recorded ingest route and both store IDs; restart replay also requires the restart record. Timestamp absence alone does not establish a cause.

Five more limits affect only what the model sees in its prompt or what search and recall return; they do not lose or copy a stored row.

- **Turns can drop out of the prompt after rejected summaries.** If two summaries in a row are rejected and the maintenance sweep runs out of time, compaction pauses for 600 seconds. While it pauses, turns that no summary covers yet can drop out of the model's prompt, and the end of the pause does not bring them back. They stay stored, and recall can still reach them. Fix release not yet set ([#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272)).
- **After a host restart, turns since the first compaction drop out of the model's view.** Only in a conversation that has a compaction child (Hermes's legacy rotating compaction, `compression.in_place: false`, now or earlier; the default in-place mode creates none): on Hermes v0.21.6 to v0.23.1 over ACP (by our reading of the source; not run on a release; seen on two pinned upstream builds), any restart of the host, clean or after a crash, resumes the conversation as it was before its first compaction. Turns since then are no longer sent to the model, and default recall (scoped to the current session) does not reach their raw rows. Their rows remain in LCM-X's store; from v0.30.1 that includes the rows of a turn interrupted by a hard kill, recovered at the next start of the conversation (#2624). This is a host defect, tracked upstream in NousResearch/hermes-agent#148047; v0.29.2 behaves the same. The #2624 recovery does not bring those turns back into the model's view, so this stays open ([#2626](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2626)).
- **`lcm_grep` searches only the first 512 KB of a saved tool output.** The rest of the file is kept but is not searched. Fix release not yet set ([#2518](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2518)).
- **A value that appears only in a tool call's input is not searchable.** The call is stored, but search does not find a value that appears only in its arguments. Fix release not yet set ([#2519](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2519)).
- **In a saved tool output, `lcm_grep` finds a query only where it appears word for word.** A quoted phrase, the same words in another order or one extra word finds nothing in a saved tool output, although message search matches such queries term by term. In the read-only MCP reader, hybrid and semantic modes do not search saved tool outputs in the default scope (an explicit `content_scope` is served by full-text search); use `mode='full_text'` there. The first part is fixed on main ([#2586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2586), [PR #2587](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2587)); the second is tracked in [#2592](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2592), with no fix release set yet.

## Qualification

This is a release candidate for testing. It is not qualified for general use yet, and v0.30.0 remains the latest stable release. As a patch release, v0.30.1 runs a smoke stage first at each release candidate, and no long row starts until it passes; then it runs the rows its diff selects. Its changes touch ingest, storage, recall and host integration, and with no class table committed every changed path selects every row class: Phase A, D1, D4/D8, D2/D3, D7 and the Phase C host cells, beside the rows every candidate runs (Phase B, the required CI checks, the Phase C soak, D5 and the upgrade-rollback roundtrip). The rows and bars that govern this train are those of the release spec on main, including the v0.30.1-only rows added in [#2690](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2690); the release branch's own copy of the spec is not a gate input. No row below has run yet. The GA notes will report each row with its receipt.

- The reliability matrix is scored with the reliability scorer from main, which expects the replies that the compaction-child recovery now stores; the v0.30.0 baseline is scored again once with the same scorer. The release branch's own copy of that scorer is not a gate input.
- Smoke stage: the reliability matrix on all seven hosts, gating on new failures; the hands-on fault-cell pairs, v0.30.0 against the candidate; Phase A, every registered tool in both postures; upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade on one store copy; D1 recall with embeddings off, fast tier; and Phase B, the independent review sweep of the v0.30.0 to rc diff: **not run yet**.
- Full suite, the CI way, at the rc tag: **not run yet**.
- Nothing lost, the certifying driven run, which measures this release's bar of 0 lost rows and 0 silent extra copies: **not run yet**.
- Phase B, the host-suite comparison on the real host builds: **not run yet**. On the two Python 3.14 builds both versions run at 4,096 open files, and the failing tests are read as a v0.30.1-only row of the release spec says.
- Phase C on the real hosts, and the local host cells: **not run yet**. Their doctor and caught-trace bars are judged by class against v0.30.0's shapes, as a v0.30.1-only row of the release spec says.
- D5-B, the two clone cells: **not run yet**, with the same kind of row for their doctor and traceback bars.
- D5, the clone run, which moved from v0.30.0 to this release ([#2647](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2647)): **not run yet**. It runs on the first candidate cut after #2647's fixes merge and its runner passes a dry run; if no candidate meets that, it is not run for this release. Before it runs, its pinned store snapshot is checked for a bare saved-output marker repeated under a reused call id in a replayed conversation, the shape of the remaining copy under [#2558](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2558). No other row can reach that shape: each full-host row starts from a fresh store, and the generated workloads never repeat a call id.
- D1 with local embeddings, with `OFF` recorded beside it, and D4/D8: **not run yet**. D8 reads a count margin per category in place of the 95% interval (rule `d8-count-margin-v2`, [#2097](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2097)).
- D7, the compaction row: **not run yet**. Its facts bar is judged against v0.30.0's recorded mean, with the same reader and summariser.
- D2, D3 and their prospective A/A: **not run** (raw verdict UNRUN, which is not green). The A/A cannot run validly until a reviewed spec change settles which summariser outcomes are failures ([#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272), [#2273](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2273), [#2274](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2274)). The GA can ship with them not green only under the conditions of the release spec's v0.30.1-only D2/D3 row, among them that D7 passes and that D5-B and Phase C find no lost row.
- The busy-session check ([#2293](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2293)): **not run yet**. It runs on this candidate against v0.30.0 and v0.29.2. This release carries one step of that work, not the fix, so a result no worse than v0.30.0 stays listed under **Known issues** and does not hold the release.
- Not run, because this diff does not select them: the D6 rows, which are recorded and never gate, apart from the `OFF` recall row that D1 records; and the two test-kit rows that v0.30.0 removed from its selection ([#2496](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2496)).
